source.title: Binary Classification of Gaussian Mixtures: Abundance of Support Vectors, Benign Overfitting, and Regularization

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how classification risk changes with feature dimension in Gaussian-mixture linear classifiers, a different setting and method from the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's own dimension sweeps and risk descriptions are recorded below. Its discussions of double descent that cite other studies are not rows. The regularization and noisy-label results do not measure the presence, shape, or location of a double-descent peak; they are not recorded as claim-version rows.
record.test_reason: The paper sweeps feature dimension p in overparameterized linear classifiers (min-norm LS and hard-margin SVM) on Gaussian-mixture data. These are its own results on whether risk keeps improving past interpolation, which bears on V4 in a new, non-deep setting. All sweeps lie in p > n, so they cover only the post-interpolation branch.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors show the max-margin SVM interpolates Gaussian-mixture data under sufficient overparameterization and SNR conditions, so it coincides with min-norm LS. They derive non-asymptotic error bounds and conditions for benign overfitting, including under label noise. They also show that optimal regularization depends on covariance structure: large τ is best for balanced spectra, while τ=0 can be optimal for bi-level spectra. They do not frame results as testing double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes linear SVM and minimum-norm least-squares classifiers on Gaussian-mixture data, using non-asymptotic bounds and simulations; it does not reproduce deep-network training or the original studies' size, epoch, and sample-size experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk trends vary with signal strength and covariance structure; the paper reports different dimension-dependent behavior in the isotropic and other Gaussian-mixture settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In the bi-level ensemble with large p, the unregularized interpolator (τ=0) outperforms ridge-regularized estimators. In the balanced ensemble, error decreases monotonically with τ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether interpolation beats optimally tuned regularization in overparameterized linear classification depends on covariance structure (spiky vs balanced spectrum).

fits_no_version.finding: With label-flip noise γ, interpolating SVM/LS risk is bounded to approach γ (benign overfitting) under stated SNR/overparameterization conditions. This is theoretical only, with no sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign overfitting of interpolating linear classifiers under label noise.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The dimension-sweep results are presented in figures without numeric error values or plotted uncertainty intervals. The reported sweeps do not establish the full curve around the interpolation point, and the study uses linear classifiers rather than deep networks.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing dimension-sweep rows were left out. Regularization and noisy-label analyses were not extracted as claim rows because they do not measure double-descent peak behavior; cited findings from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: No sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold.
The under-parameterized regime and the peak at the interpolation threshold (p≈n) are not swept. Only linear classifiers on Gaussian mixtures are studied.
No test of a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
No peak measured, so there is no test of a noise-driven peak, multiple peaks, or regularization removing a peak.
No re-plotting against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Min-norm LS (and SVM, various τ) classification error vs p in the bi-level ensemble. Settings: n=30, λ2..λp=50, λ1=10||λ||−1, ηp=0.1√50·p^0.6. The LS error approaches 0 as p grows and is best among estimators at large p.
Classification error vs p for τ/n=0,1,10,100 and the averaging estimator in the balanced ensemble, with fixed per-p signal ||η||²=0.125²p (three η configurations).

record.verdict_notes: The study is about benign overfitting, not a full double-descent sweep: all simulations use p>n, so the first descent and the interpolation peak are never observed. The record's 'challenges' label for R1–R4 was wrong: those curves show improvement past interpolation that later reverses only because SNR is held fixed as p grows, so limits_scope is appropriate. Double-descent mentions (Montanari et al., Deng et al.) are citations, not results. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 (new linear-classification setting).

versions.untested_parts: The study uses linear classifiers, not deep networks.
No risk sweep over training epochs or training time.
No experiment varying training sample size near an interpolation threshold to measure its effect on test error.
The study tests linear classifiers on Gaussian-mixture data, not a range of model classes. Its sweeps do not establish the full fall-rise-fall curve around the interpolation point.
The study discusses effective ranks and covariance summaries, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
The paper studies label noise and regularization, but does not test whether noise drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
No comparison of a second-descent curve with a curve plotted against an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: min-norm LS classifier (η̂ LS)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep feature dimension p and measure classification error
rows.note: The text describes -log(error) as increasing to a maximum and then decreasing as p increases, which corresponds to error first decreasing and then increasing; it does not describe the further error decline required by a full double-descent curve.
rows.check: The note misreads the curve. The whole x-range (p=250–1000, n=100) is past interpolation. Error first falls with p (a second-descent segment), then rises at large p because SNR ||η||² is held fixed. The peak at p≈n is not shown.

relationships.condition: Overparameterized LS/SVM; signal strength growing with p (Fig. 3, n=50, η=0.1–0.25 per entry)
relationships.reason: Classification error falls toward zero as p grows past interpolation (R5–R12). Fig. 6(b), bi-level LS, shows the same (text-based, missing row).

relation.reason: The study directly analyzes and simulates whether classification risk improves with increasing overparameterization.

tranche.reason: Own theoretical results and dimension sweeps test post-interpolation generalization in a generative Gaussian-mixture classification setting.

source_check.notes: The results establish post-interpolation behavior rather than a full threshold-spanning double-descent curve. The covariance-formula discrepancy in R5–R12 concerns an apparent source typo and does not undermine the explicitly stated qualitative trends.
